reply_text:
I've written a draft of both plans and sent it to codex-6 for their independent position. No clicks, code changes or other handoffs happen until you've seen the text we agree.

The draft is `futon2/holes/labs/wm-contract/PROOF-2b-ACTIONS-draft-2026-09-30.md` (commit `78a06c752`). It records your three rulings at the top.

**Plan A, the actions.** Eleven rows, one per step of `PROOF-2b.md` up to ⟨1⟩5, plus one new row for the click 19/20 defect (a typed author refusal must become selectable work or move selection on). Every acceptance is rewritten so it needs no click. The parts of the original ACCEPT lines that do need a live click are listed separately as deferred and are not in the plan.

**Plan B, verification before any click.** Four methods, each with what it can and cannot show:

- **Decision dry-run:** call the click's own judge in the serving JVM on live data and stop before dispatch. It shows what the next click would select.
- **Hermetic tick:** run the whole tick in a test JVM against throwaway stores, with stub seats replaying the replies recorded in clicks 13–20.
- **Sequence:** several such ticks in a row, each outcome written back before the next. This is the check for repeats after a failure.
- **Loaded-code check:** confirm the serving JVM is running what was verified.

Each check has its expected result written down before it is run, and the results go in a readiness record for you to read. Whether to run clicks after that is your decision.

**What I asked codex-6 for:**
- agree, amend or strike each row, with reasons;
- whether any method only tests its own stubs;
- what they would require before agreeing a click could run;
- anything the draft gets wrong about the code.

One thing I don't yet know: whether the judge can be called in the serving JVM without writing to stores or traces. The draft makes that the first discovery item.
